page0.text:
This happened ten years ago.
In the middle of a blazing town, I chased the responsibility of being the only survivor.

page2.text:
I've never forgotten, not even once.
The price I paid for surviving is to make sure that this scene never happens again.

page4.text:
I swore an oath.
I swore to myself that I'd always do the right thing, like my old man.
That's what Shirou Emiya has spent his life doing.
I got this far allowing my own life to be used by others, so that I could proudly face those who couldn't be saved.

page5.text:
I understand that all too well.
I do.
And yet...

page7.text:
I know the main culprit.
You know who you should defeat.
The black sun.
You have to kill that Shadow which appeared in the sky that day, before it happens again.

page8.text:
"...Ahh."
Remember what you've lived for, all this time.
You affirmed your way of life to save those who wish to be saved, and to help innocent people who get caught in tragedies.
And if you're going to reject it all now for just one woman...

page9.text: "If you're going to betray it all..."

page10.text: Then Shirou Emiya must pass judgment on himself.

page11.text:
"...It's morning."
I wake up from my slumber.
It's bright outside, and past seven o'clock.

page12.text:
...
My body feels heavy.
My limbs feel numb.
My sluggish head can't quite remember who I am. Maybe my blood isn't flowing yet.

page13.text:
"...Oh, right. Sakura, what do you want for breakfast?"
I pat Sakura, who's sleeping next to me.
Strangely, all I remember is that we went to sleep next to each other.
The fact that the girl I love is sleeping next to me must be far more important than silly questions like, "Who am I?"

page14.text:
"Sakura, it's morning. You'd better get up or else there's gonna be a lot of trouble with breakfast and Tohsaka and everything."
I touch her shoulder a couple more times.
...Sakura feels cold.
I don't mean her attitude. She's physically cold and hard to the touch.

page15.text:
"...Sakura?"
In a haze, I get up and look around the room.

page16.text:
...
She's not here.
The sensation of sleeping together and holding her hand tightly so she won't go anywhere is gone. Sakura isn't in the room.

page17.text:
"Sakura!"
She's nowhere to be found.
Her room is silent and unused.

page18.text:
There's nobody in the living room.
"Hah... ngh!"
I can't move my body very well. I stub a toe on the table as I try to get around it.
I trip and fall, using the wall to get back up, and I go to the hallway.
"—. —, —"
Am I panicking?
Nothing feels wrong with my body, but I can't calm down.
Why am I panicking? What am I anxious about?
I try to put it into words, but I end up getting lost in thought for ten seconds.

page19.text:
Am I unable to think right now?
Or does something I've already thought of just fail to come to mind?
The bloodflow in my just-awakened head is poor, and I can't tell which it is.

page20.text:
"—, —, —"
I can't remember what I want to do.
But I see Sakura's shoes by the front door and breathe a sigh of relief.
Tohsaka's shoes aren't here. Illya's shoes are.
What that means is...

page23.text:
"Oh, right. Sakura must be at home, while Tohsaka's the only one outside."
So that's why I feel relieved.
Sakura hasn't gone out anywhere.
Okay, I'm starting to connect the dots.
Basically, Sakura woke up first. She must have washed up, made breakfast, trained in the dojo, and did laundry in the backyard.

page24.text:
"Guess I was worried for nothing."
I sigh and turn back to the living room.
"Huh, Shirou!?"
Tohsaka comes running in from the front door.

page25.text:
"What's up, Tohsaka? On a morning walk?"
"Why would I be taking it easy like that!? We'll talk later!
Sakura collapsed outside, so carry her in! I'll get ready to give her first aid!"
